News and Features

June 24, 2026

A new era for ancient studies at UCLA

With an $11 million gift from alum Jeffrey Cunard, the university will launch a new center in the humanities division to support and expand scholarship on ancient cultures and the world of antiquity

Source: UCLA Newsroom

  • June 24, 2026

    Neanderthals in Western Europe were doing well right before they went extinct

    Using DNA extracted from the bones of 27 specimens who lived around 45,000 years ago, UCLA researchers found the population was genetically healthy and well-connected with other groups

    Source: UCLA Newsroom

  • June 24, 2026

    Inside the UCLA Health lab testing World Cup and Olympic athletes

    With 1,248 players from 48 countries competing across the U.S., Mexico and Canada, UCLA’s Olympic Analytical Laboratory is focused on ensuring the World Cup isn’t decided by syringes

    Source: UCLA Newsroom

  • June 24, 2026

    How childhood adversity can rewire our cells, with lifelong health effects

    Scientists at UCLA have discovered how abuse and neglect affect mitochondria in distinct ways, which may explain the lasting biological toll of childhood poverty and trauma

    Source: UCLA Newsroom
